1 big thing: Trump says he's at Iran crossroads
 
Photo illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Photos: Getty Images

President Trump believes he's approaching a critical juncture in the Iran war over whether to restart massive attacks in an effort to end the conflict, he told Axios' Barak Ravid today.

  • Trump said: "I have a big decision coming up. Do I want to go in and annihilate them [the Iranian regime] or do I not? It's a big decision. Anything could happen with me."

🇺🇳 Trump's comments come ahead of a planned meeting with leaders from six Gulf countries — Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman — on the sidelines of next week's UN General Assembly in New York.

  • The meeting could shape the next phase of the war. If Trump wants to resume major combat operations, he'll need buy-in from his regional allies.
  • The president has said several times in recent days that the war will end soon. Some U.S. officials warn that the conflict has settled into an unsustainable, neither-war-nor-peace stalemate, and they believe that Trump could return to major combat operations after the midterms if a deal isn't reached by then.

🌍 Trump made clear in the interview that he wants to use the UN meeting to hear directly from regional allies about the war's next steps.

  • He said: "I want to find out where they are and how they are doing. We have been very protective of them."
  • Trump declined to say whether he'll decide on the path forward before or after the midterms.

2. ⛽️ No relief for energy prices
 
Data: FactSet. Chart: Axios Markets/Matt Phillips

Markets are coming around to the view that energy prices will stay high well into next year, Axios' Matt Phillips reports.

  • Brent crude futures contracts for April 2027 jumped to more than $85 a barrel this week.
  • That's the highest since the war in Iran began in February, and higher than at the peak for oil prices back in early May.

💥 The upswing comes after drone attacks on an alternative crude oil export route to the Red Sea and on a key pipeline.

  • The latest prices for Brent oil futures set for delivery over the next six months or so have jumped higher recently. (That's the pink line in the chart above, compared with the same contract prices a week, a month and a year ago.)

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney (left) and U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham attend a soccer match together yesterday in Liverpool, England. Photo: Paul Cooper/WPA Pool/Getty Images
  1. 🇨🇦 Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney embraced the prospect of his country becoming the European Union's first associate member amid a rift with the U.S. Go deeper.
  2. 🚔 The White House is pulling Lance Schroyer's stalled nomination to lead ICE. His limited immigration experience created tension between Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and border czar Tom Homan, along with other MAGA figures. Go deeper.
  3. 🤑 The SEC is opening the door for crypto-style trading of U.S. stocks, allowing tokenized shares to trade on blockchain-based venues under a new regulatory exemption. What to know.
  4. 🏈 Steve Belichick — son of head coach Bill Belichick — has resigned from UNC's football program after an investigation into its "culture and climate," The Athletic reports. Gift link.
 
 
4. 📸 Pic to go: Kennedy Center meme
 
Photo: Brendan Smialowski/AFP via Getty Images

AFP photographer Brendan Smialowski captured this image of President Trump, aboard Air Force One last night, examining a meme related to the potential demolition of the Kennedy Center.

  • Trump warned yesterday that the iconic performing arts venue could be "ripped down" if his administration doesn't receive "recognition" on the building.

The latest: A federal judge today ordered the Kennedy Center to provide 30 days' notice before making any major physical changes to the building.
